item.title: Governmental Affairs Associate
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.

The Association County Commissioners of Georgia (ACCG) is a nonprofit instrumentality of Georgia's county governments, serving as the consensus-building, training, and legislative organization for all 159 county governments in the state since 1914. The Governmental Affairs Associate coordinates policy development processes, researches and shapes state and federal policy, and advocates on behalf of ACCG membership. The position reports to the Director of Governmental Affairs.

Key responsibilities: Assist with coordinating policy development for key functional areas of county government; promote the Association's legislative initiatives and positions and represent the association before the Georgia General Assembly, Congress, and state and federal agencies; monitor, review, analyze, summarize, and report on legislation at the state and federal level to determine impact on counties; receive and respond to inquiries from counties, legislators, state agencies, media, and the public; prepare written material for the Association's magazine, newsletters, social media, and handbooks; work with ACCG Policy Committee Chairpersons to develop meeting agendas; serve on federal, state, and regional advisory committees; and facilitate district visits and meetings. Position requires travel within Georgia with occasional overnight travel.

Qualifications: Bachelor's degree with coursework in political science, criminal justice, law, planning, public administration, or a related field, plus 1–3 years of experience in public policy with extensive writing, communication, and public speaking experience. Must have thorough knowledge of county government in Georgia and demonstrated ability to build relationships with elected officials, media, and diverse stakeholders.

Salary starts from $70,000 annually. ACCG is an equal opportunity employer.

item.title: Researcher
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.

The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) is a non-partisan, non-profit public policy research organization dedicated to advancing an informed understanding of military affairs through reliable research, trusted analysis, and innovative education. ISW is committed to improving the nation's ability to execute military operations and respond to emerging threats to achieve U.S. strategic objectives. ISW researchers produce timely open-source intelligence analysis for policymakers, warfighters, and the general public on conflicts including Russia-Ukraine, the Middle East, and China-related security issues.

The Researcher will conduct open-source research and analysis of geo-strategic dynamics affecting U.S. national security interests. Responsibilities include: conducting detailed open-source intelligence analysis of current conflicts and security threats; writing and publishing analytical reports and short-form intelligence products; editing and overseeing daily written products to meet institutional writing standards; collaborating with the research team to generate intelligence products; and supporting the planning, preparation, and execution of public events and private briefings. ISW researchers work directly with senior analysts and contribute to shaping policy recommendations.

Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in a field related to ISW's core mission (international relations, political science, area studies, national security) is required; a master's degree is preferred. Demonstrated analytical writing ability and expertise in a relevant geographic or functional area (e.g., Russia, Middle East, China, defense policy) is required. Critical language skills (Russian, Arabic, Mandarin, Hebrew, Ukrainian, Persian, etc.) are a plus. ISW provides formal professional development in war studies, analytic methods, and policy writing. This is a full-time, in-person role in Washington, DC.

item.title: Researcher / Sr. Researcher, Energy Systems & International Development
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.

Mathematica applies expertise at the intersection of data, methods, policy, and practice to improve well-being around the world, collaborating closely with public- and private-sector partners to translate big questions into deep insights. The company is 100% employee-owned and conducts work in health, education, early childhood, nutrition, employment, disability, and international development. This Researcher or Senior Researcher position will support anticipated evaluations in the energy sector in low- or middle-income countries (LMICs), designing and executing user-focused evaluations that help donors, practitioners, and policymakers improve programs and make data-driven decisions.

Key responsibilities include: serving as technical expert on evaluations of diverse energy sector investments (grid expansion, off-grid systems, utility performance, renewable energy, energy efficiency, and energy systems planning); advising on data sources and coordinating with technical stakeholders to obtain administrative and grid-level data; integrating open-source and widely available energy/climate data platforms into MEL work; conducting key informant interviews with program participants, engineers, utility staff, policymakers, and donors; providing written summaries and analyses of findings; and performing landscape assessments, case studies, and political economy analyses of the energy sector in LMICs.

Qualifications: A postgraduate or doctoral degree in electrical engineering, physics, environmental/climate science, energy economics, energy policy, or related field is required. Minimum five years of experience working in the energy sector in a low- or middle-income country, including deep understanding of policy/regulatory frameworks, generation, transmission, distribution technologies, and energy finance is required. Familiarity with evaluation methodologies and quantitative/qualitative research methods is needed. Fluency in English; proficiency in French strongly preferred. Willingness to travel to project locations required. Note: If an offer is extended, it is contingent upon successful award of relevant work.

Salary: $120,000–$135,000 (Researcher) or $140,000–$155,000 (Senior Researcher), plus annual bonus and comprehensive ESOP/benefits package.

item.title: Sr. Global Trade Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 6/27/2026.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars — including Falcon, Starship, Dragon, and Starlink programs. The Sr. Global Trade Analyst will support SpaceX's global trade compliance team on these programs, based in SpaceX's Washington, DC office.

As a Sr. Global Trade Analyst, you will support SpaceX's global trade compliance team on Falcon, Starship, Dragon, and Starlink programs, with a focus on export control matters. You will work closely with attorneys, other legal and compliance professionals, and engineers to ensure that SpaceX complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and is able to conduct launches and other operations in a timely fashion. Key responsibilities include: conducting research on U.S. federal statutes, regulations, directives, and guidance related to export laws (EAR, ITAR, OFAC); reviewing technical documentation and advising on export classification and licensing requirements; supporting internal compliance investigations; managing export and import licensing applications and correspondence with government agencies; and helping define and implement global standards for trade compliance data within item master records.

Qualifications: A bachelor's degree is required; a degree in international affairs, legal studies, engineering, or a related discipline is preferred. 4–6 years of relevant experience in global trade compliance, export control, or national security law is required, with demonstrated focus on customs and import compliance. Strong knowledge of ITAR, EAR, and related U.S. export regulations is essential. SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Note: an active security clearance may be required for certain mission-critical work.

For full position details and to apply, please visit the original posting.

item.title: Strategic Accounts Associate (Public Sector)
item.description:
Kharon operates at the intersection of global security threats and international commerce, turning complex global-security data into intelligence that clients can operationalize to understand and manage the risks in their business relationships — from financial crimes and sanctions to export controls and threat identification. Its products serve many of the world's leading global financial and multinational institutions. The Strategic Accounts Associate (Public Sector) reports to the Senior Leadership team for the Public Sector and is central to the sales team's operations and the company's growth, working closely with the Sales and Marketing teams to identify leads and conduct business intelligence research that prepares them for public-sector client and prospect meetings.

Responsibilities: support the Sales team in preparing for client and prospective-client meetings; conduct sophisticated public-sector intelligence research on target agencies and geographies, with a specialized focus on sanctions, forced-labor exposure, and financial-crime regulatory frameworks, to uncover blind spots and opportunities; proactively map high-value entry points, decision-makers, and expansion opportunities across the public sector; collaborate with Kharon's marketing and research teams to support participation in industry events and conferences, including drafting and editing proprietary material and collateral; provide end-to-end support on high-stakes proposals, RFPs, and presentations, from slide-deck narrative through tracking next steps; and leverage advanced AI tools (including Gemini and/or Claude) to streamline business-development workflows, automate lead-generation research, and prepare high-impact briefs, predictive insights, and tailored materials.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree, preferably in Business, International Relations, Political Science, or a related field; 2+ years of professional experience (not internships) in business development, sales support, research, or operations in the public/federal sector, focused on SaaS or professional services; academic or professional exposure to global security, international relations, financial crime, compliance, or regulatory environments; a foundational understanding of compliance frameworks such as anti-money laundering (AML), illicit financing, sanctions regimes, and ESG standards; strong research and analytical skills; proficiency in PowerPoint/Google Slides, Excel/Sheets, and CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot); excellent written and verbal communication with experience drafting proposals, pitch decks, and sales collateral; and strong organization, judgment, initiative, and integrity.

Logistics and benefits: Full-time, hybrid role based in Washington, D.C., requiring frequent in-office attendance. Base salary range $70,000 to $85,000 (exclusive of potential bonuses, commissions, or benefits). Benefits include fully sponsored medical, dental, and vision; medical and dependent-care FSA; 401(k) + Roth with matching and immediate vesting; and paid time off plus 11 paid holidays. Application deadline: July 31, 2026; apply at www.kharon.com.

item.title: Consultant - Atlanta Metro Area
item.description:

CCS Fundraising is an international strategic fundraising firm that has partnered with nonprofits for transformational change for 76 years, planning, managing, and implementing programs and initiatives that achieve fundraising goals and mission impact. CCS provides tailored support to more than 700 nonprofit organizations annually, with over 500 professionals across 18 offices throughout the United States and Europe; its services include campaign management, strategy/evaluation/planning, interim development management, learning and leadership development, and data analytics. As a Consultant based in the Atlanta metro area, you will have direct access to leaders in the field and work across philanthropic sectors with clients, colleagues, and philanthropists.

Projects may include: developing work plans and materials for campaign planning studies and development assessments; conducting analysis of clients through review of fundraising performance and interviews with the organization's executives, volunteer leaders, and donors; preparing fundraising campaign materials, including strategic plans, operating materials, case statements, and major gift proposals; conducting in-depth prospect research; crafting individual cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies; and writing and delivering high-impact presentations and materials.

The ideal candidate is highly self-motivated and passionate, with fundraising experience or transferable skills in consulting, communications, marketing, and strategic planning, and can: successfully lead and manage projects from inception to conclusion; apply critical and strategic thinking to quickly identify the crux of a problem; communicate clearly and logically, articulating strategies to a variety of audiences; remain open-minded to new ideas; and thrive in a mission-oriented environment working across philanthropic sectors. Qualifications include excellent quantitative analytical skills, keen business sense, exceptional interpersonal skills and the ability to work collaboratively with staff, volunteers, and donors, outstanding organizational skills to manage multiple tasks, strong storytelling and public-speaking skills, a professional demeanor, and computer proficiency. The ability to temporarily relocate for regional assignments may be required.

Logistics: Full-time, hybrid, based in Atlanta, GA. Salary range: $60,000 to $120,000, with exact salary varying within the range based on years of relevant experience and education. A cover letter is required. CCS cannot sponsor work visas (including H-1B); candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without current or future visa sponsorship. CCS is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

item.title: Associate China Corporate & Investment Risk Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 7/15/2026.

ANSER (Analytic Services Inc.) enhances national and homeland security by strengthening public institutions, providing thought leadership on complex issues through independent analysis and delivering practical, useful solutions; as a not-for-profit established for public service, it measures success by the impact of its service. The Associate China Corporate & Investment Risk Analyst supports the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Industrial Base Policy (IBP), Global Investment and Economic Security Directorate (GIES), supporting the development, research, and coordination of the Department of Defense Section 1260H program identifying Chinese military companies.

Day-to-day responsibilities: support open-source and classified research on companies for potential inclusion on the 1260H list, including collecting data on ownership structures, affiliations, and business activities; assist with coordination of the annual Section 1260H requirement and related list development with DoD and interagency stakeholders; support drafting of company due-diligence summaries, analytic notes, and supporting documentation; maintain and update processes and documentation related to 1260H list publication and review; support the development and tracking of notice and appeals processes; assist in coordinating correspondence from listed companies, Congress, and interagency stakeholders; compile and consolidate inputs across GIES organizations and DoD stakeholders for program responses and reporting; support preparation of responses to congressional inquiries and reporting requirements; analyze statutes, congressional actions, and legislative developments for potential impacts on GIES programs; contribute to drafting policy documents and guidance related to foreign investment risk and industrial base security; support preparation of briefing materials, reports, and analytic products for senior DoD leadership; maintain records and databases supporting the 1260H process; and support research on foreign investment review, supply chain resilience, and risk monitoring.

Required qualifications: an active TS/SCI-eligible clearance; a bachelor's degree; 2+ years of experience in International Affairs, Diplomacy, Economics, Finance, National Security, or Business Administration; demonstrated analytic and writing skills with ability to prepare reports and assessments; experience conducting business analysis, research studies, or requirements analysis to support policy, regulatory, or organizational initiatives; and experience analyzing trends, regulatory developments, and business conditions to identify risks. Preferred: experience in international affairs or China-related economic or security analysis, Mandarin language proficiency, and experience researching corporate ownership structures and international investment activity.

Logistics: Full-time, based in Alexandria, VA. Salary is not stated in the posting; applicants are asked to provide their salary expectations. ANSER is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

item.title: Policy Analyst (Children and Families)
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 7/15/2026.

Founded in 1908, the National Governors Association (NGA) is the bipartisan organization of governors from the 55 states, territories, and commonwealths; its mission is to share best practices, address issues of national and state interest, and drive innovative solutions that improve state government and support the principles of federalism. NGA's Center for Best Practices is the policy and research arm that helps governors develop and implement solutions to public policy challenges. The Policy Analyst (Children and Families) reports to the Program Director (Children and Families) and supports governors on a variety of human services programs and benefits — including those focused on increasing economic mobility (such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program, and Medicaid), strengthening families, supporting early childhood education and care, protecting children, and improving youth mental health — as well as the workforce and systems used to administer these programs.

Key responsibilities: organize and facilitate state learning opportunities, including virtual, in-person, and hybrid events such as workshops, seminars, meetings, and presentations; facilitate panel discussions, state strategy sessions, and other events for governors, senior state policy staff, and key stakeholders; provide state technical assistance for multiple program and policy issues; provide best-practice information and consultative support to governors and their senior advisors in response to requests; develop blog posts, white papers, issue briefs, presentations, and memos on policy issues and best practices relevant to governors and senior state policymakers; and build and maintain relationships with high-level policymakers and key stakeholders.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree, preferably in public policy or a related field, and one to three years working in policies and programs within the children and families portfolio. Knowledge could include helping governors, their staff, and executive-branch appointees design and implement evidence-based policies; experience working with governors, in federal or state agencies, or in nonprofit organizations is preferred, and commensurate lived experience is also considered. The ideal candidate can demonstrate foundational content knowledge in federal and state policy in the issue area, support multiple technical-assistance projects, manage competing project deadlines, synthesize complex issues into audience-appropriate recommendations, work independently and problem-solve, support and organize events, demonstrate strong analytical skills interpreting and re-purposing research for policymakers, and communicate effectively with policy-making audiences. Knowledge of MS Office and willingness to travel as necessary are expected.

Logistics: Full-time, exempt, onsite in Washington, DC. Salary range: $70,000 to $85,000 annually. Applicants should apply online via NGA's career site and include a resume and a portfolio of their best work.
